title: Polaris watch handover coda — 2027-04-06
content:
Polaris watch 04:00-12:00 UTC — handover notes and follow-ups

Shift summary:
- Handover from night team: briefed on degraded embeddings throughput between 02:10-03:05 UTC; persisted KV cache thrash observed. Night team mitigated via scaling burst pool + re-route to fallback quantized model (q8) for low-priority jobs.
- My shift scope: 04:00-12:00 UTC, primary on-call for inferred-hosted cluster eu-west-1, secondary for dedicated pools.
- Overall: user-facing latency returned to target by 05:30 UTC. No customer-facing pages were opened but we had a short blip in /generate API error rate (5xx spike to 2.3%).

Incidents and timelines:
1) Incident SRE-421 (medium) — embeddings throughput degradation
   - Detected: 02:08 UTC by autoscale alert (embedding-queue-depth > 200 for 5m).
   - User impact: background batch embeddings (non-critical) experienced increased tail latency ~5-8x. Hosted synchronous queries saw a small uptick in p95 for embeddings-only routes.
   - What we tried: night team increased dedicated pool from 8->12 GPUs (burst capacity), enabled prefix-KV cache warm-up on pool, temporarily routed low-priority batches to q8 variant.
   - Observed root cause (initial hypothesis): KV cache eviction storm triggered by a restart loop in cache-writer sidecar (OOM due to recent JVM heap growth after monitoring change).
   - Current status: mitigated (no ongoing impact). Owner: Priya Singh. Follow-up ticket SRE-421 in Jira.

2) Small error spike — /generate 5xx blip (short)
   - Time: 04:18-04:25 UTC
   - Metric: 5xx rate from 0.02% -> 2.3% during window.
   - Quick triage: correlated with a rolling deploy to model-router service (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1893). Rollout was paused at 04:20 due to elevated errors.
   - Remediation: rolled back the router change at 04:23; errors normalized by 04:25.
   - Action: add stricter healthcheck gating + canary sample size to the router rollout runbook. Owner: Omar Ruiz. Jira: SRE-427.

Operational notes and commands run (cheatsheet)
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=model-router --wide  # check router rollout
- kubectl -n prod logs deployment/cache-writer --since=2h | grep -i oom
- /opt/sre/scripts/restart_cachewriter.sh (deployed as temporary mitigation)
- curl -H 'x-api-key: x' https://api.redwood.io/v1/health  # smoke test after rollback

Dashboards & graphs reviewed:
- embeddings queue depth (console.redwood.io/d/embeddings-queue) — peak at 02:12 UTC
- model-router canary dashboard — error spike co-located with PR rollout
- infra memory heap histograms for cache-writer sidecar — upward drift starting 2027-04-05 22:00 UTC

Runbook gaps discovered (needs edits)
- cache-writer runbook: no guidance for JVM heap regression test or safe restart window. Add steps: graceful drain, check persistent KV miss-rate post-restart, increase livenessProbe threshold for sidecar.
- router rollout runbook: current canary gating only looks at pod readiness; add request-level error rate and latency checks (p90/p99) and a minimum canary traffic sample of 3%.
- scaling policy: autoscaler alphav2 responded correctly but scaling cooldown too short for embedding backpressure patterns. Investigate a 10m cooldown in steady-state tests.

Action items / follow-ups (with owners and tentative due dates)
- SRE-421: Root cause analysis for cache-writer OOM + mitigation plan (Priya Singh) — due 2027-04-12
- SRE-427: Update model-router rollout runbook (Omar Ruiz) — due 2027-04-09
- Infra: Add heap regression test to CI for cache-writer image (Eng-Infra: Ben K.) — due 2027-04-14
- Observability: Create alert for sustained KV miss-rate > 1% for 10m (Monitoring: Linh) — due 2027-04-08
- Post-incident review doc: short postmortem draft + timeline (Maya Chen) — due 2027-04-10

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Night team mentioned a config change in the monitoring agent on 2027-04-05 at 21:40 that increased heap usage. Who approved that change? Need to surface in RCA.
- We should validate that q8 fallback quality is acceptable for our customers; Product asked for a short quality check across 50 random samples. Requesting product review (tag: @product-embeddings).

Communication / escalation notes:
- No SEV declared. Customer success not notified for page. Internal Slack thread: #sre-ops (link above).
- If we see > 10% sustained embedding queue increase or p95 embeddings > 2s for 15m, escalate to SEV-2 and notify on-call manager.

Runbook edits I will push (short checklist):
- cache-writer: add graceful-restart steps + memory-config rollback snippet + test commands
- model-router: add canary gating (error-rate + latency p99) + rollback checklist + rollback smoke endpoints
- autoscaler: document cooldown recommendations and test procedure

Notes to next shift (12:00-20:00 UTC)
- Monitor SRE-421 ticket. Priya will post interim findings by 10:00 UTC.
- Watch for any reappearance of 5xx after 04:25; if >0.5% sustained over 5m, call Omar and start rollback of latest router changes.
- Validate that cache-writer sidecar image with lowered heap (pending PR) is on canary by EOD.

Attachments & pointers:
- Jira SRE-421: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-421
- Router PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1893
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood.io/dashboards/latency/polaris-04-06
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0SREWATCH/p1634829

Quick closure note:
- No customer outages. Two mitigations (burst scaling + router rollback) prevented escalation. Several runbook gaps identified — prioritized on the board.

Maya Chen
SRE — Polaris watch
Handoff time: 12:00 UTC
